question: Should ClawHub add a first-class SKILL.md capability manifest for skills, and what schema, authority model, and advisory-to-required rollout should it use?
rationale: This changes the public skill trust contract and security review boundary; source inspection confirms the gap, but automation cannot choose the permanent schema or rollout policy safely.

options.title: Adopt advisory manifest first
options.body: Define the schema in specs, parse and expose it as advisory metadata, and let ClawScan flag declared-versus-observed mismatches before making it required.

options.title: Defer until scanner policy settles
options.body: Keep env/install metadata plus current ClawScan coherence checks for now, accepting that there is no author-declared baseline for network, filesystem, execution, or secret access yet.

options.title: Require manifests for new submissions
options.body: Make new skill submissions provide the capability block once the schema is documented, with explicit legacy and false-positive transition policy.

recommendation.title: Adopt advisory manifest first
recommendation.body: Define the schema in specs, parse and expose it as advisory metadata, and let ClawScan flag declared-versus-observed mismatches before making it required.

likelyOwner.reason: CODEOWNERS and recent history route the schema/security prompt surfaces most likely to carry this decision to Patrick-Erichsen.
